title: Post-processing a landscape with selective color and layered depth in Photoshop (windy scene workflow)
summary: This video walk-through documents a landscape post-processing workflow focused on creating depth and color separation through non-destructive editing in Photoshop. The presenter begins with framing and crop decisions suited to wind, then builds a baseline by suppressing highlights and extracting shadow detail to form a controllable canvas. He demonstrates a background-first approach using Camera Raw adjustments, then introduces selective color and precise masking to separate foreground, mid-ground, and distant elements. Key techniques include color separation via Selective Color and 50-150 adjustments, hard- and soft-edged masking for layer isolation, content-aware removal of distractions, and a disciplined, non-destructive save strategy that preserves multiple versions. The session emphasizes iterative, partial adjustments (dodge/burn, saturation, hue shifts) and emphasizes that most changes are local and layered rather than global, culminating in a scene with a clearly defined focal point and believable depth.

sections.title: Framing and crop strategy under wind
sections.description: The speaker suggests shooting wider and cropping to create a vertical composition that keeps critical elements in focus, noting that wind makes focus stacking impractical for the scene and comparing different frame options to identify a composition with tree framing and red accents.

sections.title: Initial tonal setup and non-destructive baseline
sections.description: The presenter outlines darkening the overall image and suppressing highlights to reveal shadow detail, then importing into Photoshop to begin recording a full history of edits with an expanded history states setting, framing the workflow as non-destructive from the outset.

sections.title: Background-first adjustments and selective color introduction
sections.description: The workflow shifts to RAW-based adjustments, starting with a large White’s adjustment to influence the background, then modifying color balance and exposure, and finally introducing selective color concepts as a preface to local color control.

sections.title: Color separation, masking, and depth creation
sections.description: A core portion shows color separation to push reds and greens apart, using the 50-150 rule to make a color pop. The speaker demonstrates masking techniques (hard-edge for precise edges, soft-edge for gradual blends) to isolate foreground, mid-ground, and mountains, creating perceived depth and layered lighting effects.

sections.title: Finishing, non-destructive save strategy, and philosophy
sections.description: The closing section emphasizes finishing touches (dodging/burning, light steering, minor hue/tint tweaks) and the importance of saving multiple non-destructive versions to revisit decisions later. The presenter reinforces a philosophy of incremental, non-destructive edits and speed-oriented post-processing.
